sections.title: Market
items: Feed posts have a Copy link button and a link to the post's public page on the website, which anyone can open without signing in.

sections.title: Projects
items: Pull requests show a green, orange or red merge status button at the top, a compact icon-based Reviewers list, and no longer repeat the repository's Fork and Star bar.
Issues have an Assign button next to Comment, and contributors can take a second issue once they have a pull request open for the first.
The pull request review prompt now links a working diff and a plain-text page with every comment, and asks for feedback written to the author, or a short approval when nothing needs to change.
Instances can pin the repositories shown in Top repositories and choose how many forks each row shows.

sections.title: Chat
items: Chat now lives at one address, /chat: the dashboard's Chat link and old /dashboard/chat links open it, and the people list shows each member's past-year activity under their name.
A message from someone signed in on a new phone or browser no longer stays labelled Guest: it switches to their account name as soon as the server confirms the device.

sections.title: Agents
items: The composer hides its character count until a prompt nears the limit, then shows it in orange and red.

Claude Code agents on the desktop now take their name from their Claude Code session and follow its renames, ask for tool permissions, plan approval and MCP input in the transcript or a small window instead of refusing the call, list their running sub-sessions with a Stop button, and can be renamed from the agent list.

sections.title: World
items: Where two roads meet open land at the edge of the town's hexagons, the outer road now curves smoothly from one into the next as a three-way junction, and bikes can ride straight through the curve.
Bikes riding around the outer edge of the world now stay on the outer road at each junction, and only head back in when you turn toward the inside.
You can drag the chat box anywhere in the World by the grip at its left edge (double-click it to put it back), and the last two messages now fit in it without being cut off.

sections.title: iPhone
items: With Diagnostics on, the status dots now really show above the Dynamic Island, and your desktop and node lights sit just under the clock.
With Diagnostics on, your desktop and node lights now sit just above the clock with a little more room, and the diagnostic charts sit above the battery, each filled in under its line.

sections.title: Android
items: On Android, every agent page pins the last thing you wrote to the agent above its transcript; swipe the card sideways to move through your earlier and later prompts.
On Android, the terminal's keys fit on screen in two rows, a Ctrl key sends any Ctrl combination, and scrolling up to read earlier output no longer jumps back to the bottom.
On Android, Settings > Appearance can match the instance's theme, so the app wears the colours the instance's admin picked.
On Android, Home shows a spinner on each icon whose count is loading instead of a loading bar, keeps the repository counts from last time, and its long-press menu has Refresh everything.
On Android Home, the number on each icon sits beside the icon instead of covering the name of the icon above, and the update dot is smaller.
On Android, with Status Page installed, tiny status dots sit in a thin strip under the status bar on every screen.

On Android, Settings > Data saves the home screen layout, news reader subscriptions and app settings to your ForkMesh account, encrypted, and lists everything ForkMesh keeps about you with a full download and per-item delete.
On Android, DJ Studio's AUTO DJ plays a related song people liked on the next deck, originals first, and a shake loads a new pick.
On Android, DJ Studio decks have a Repeat button that loops the song tightly, jumping from where the sound ends back to where it starts.
On Android, the CRM shows each email's opens, clicks, read time, scroll depth, slide reach and the reader's mail app.
On Android, Genie auto-send can ask the paired desktop's Claude Code or Codex to write the email.
On Android, ping notifications lead with who acted and where, with what they wrote straight under it.
On Android, New project loads the checked instance's logo and can quick-add an instance from the ForkMesh directory.
On Android, a walk shows as a live notification with its time, steps and distance, on the lock screen too, and stays when you lock the phone mid-walk.
On Android, Agents Eagle rows drop the left agent dot and show a tile with a green and red churn border, a file count and status dot pill, and blinking background-task dots.

sections.title: Desktop
items: On Linux, the app menu and dock show the new ForkMesh icon with its transparent background, even on installs from before the logo changed.

Titles and small print in the fleet view, process list, query inspector, core node dialogs and other desktop panels now follow your font size setting, and the desktop log no longer fills with "Point size <= 0" font warnings.
Merge all now pulls pull request branches from the cloud before starting, and explains when a pull request's patch no longer applies.

sections.title: Other improvements
items: Administrators can turn on an automated AI review that posts a first-pass review comment on pull requests, using Cloudflare Workers AI.
Bots and system accounts such as Actions, runners, the git node and the AI reviewer now have their own avatars.
A mention or reply notification now opens the exact comment, and Home's repository rows show their fork count.

sections.title: Market
items: Every Market package has its own page on forkmesh.com, with its details, README, ratings and an install button, and its share link now opens that page.
Video Mix DJ Studio can repeat a deck, so one song plays over and over until you turn it off.
On iPhone, Video Mix DJ Studio's Repeat now really loops the song, and starts it again as soon as the sound ends, skipping the silence at both ends for a tight loop.

sections.title: Calls
items: Every call and Office conversation now shows a small live quality pill with signal bars, a voice waveform and the delay; tap it for live network and video charts.

A small round button next to the call quality pill turns red when your call has a problem; press it to see what is wrong, how to fix it, and a prompt for your AI assistant that gets better with every call.
Face filters now keep up with you: the face follows your head with much less lag, the lips move with your speech, and the filtered camera runs at 30 frames a second.

sections.title: Projects
items: ChatGPT and other AI assistants can now read a pull request link: the page includes the description, the conversation and the diff, and adding .diff to the address gives the raw diff.
The web dashboard works again: a merge earlier today had left its script unable to load, which broke repository pages, the Actions tab and pull requests.
A pull request's merge box now lists each check with its state and log, and says when checks are waiting for a maintainer's approval.

Issue and pull request pings now say what happened, such as who approved, closed or assigned which item, and link straight to it; the issue sidebar now tells a repository owner they are receiving notifications, and Unsubscribe really stops them.
Public repositories can back themselves up to the Internet Archive every day, week or month from repository Settings, using your own archive.org keys.
The desktop pull request list marks a pull whose code is not on this computer with a faded cloud icon, and its hover text names the local branch that holds the code when it is.

sections.title: Chat
items: Edits, reactions, typing and deletes in direct messages now reach only the person you are talking to, on iPhone, Android and desktop.
Webhook posts in public channels notify everyone at most once every ten minutes, and each account can create up to 20 channels.
Direct messages and private channels always go through the server's member-checked rooms, and the shared room carries only public messages; nobody can post, edit or delete as someone else.
Account names in chat are checked with the server, so an unverified sender shows as a guest, and a bot reply shows who asked for it.
Private channels can take webhooks, and webhook messages are marked server-visible.
Blocking someone now also stops their direct messages, pushes and calls at the server.
#mesh says that anyone nearby can read it and no longer shares your account name.

sections.title: Agents
items: The pinned last prompt above an agent's transcript no longer leaves an empty box under it on the phone, you can swipe it left and right to go through earlier and later prompts, and the desktop app and the website's agent session pages now pin it too.

Desktop agents can now offer to start a new session for side work, list and message your other agents and runners, send you notifications, click and type in their browser windows, and open small interactive widgets in ForkMesh, like Claude Code's desktop app.
The agent header shows your five most-used actions with the rest under a More menu, and the agent list's toolbar does the same, so neither overlaps or runs off the edge in a narrow window.

The prompt box shows the last three lines of the conversation it will reply to, its follow-up button now reads chat, the branch, cloud and vibe switches are icons on the right with an outline when on, and the send buttons have icons.
In the iPhone terminal, every key now fits on screen, a Ctrl key sends any Ctrl combination such as Ctrl+X then Ctrl+S, and scrolling up to read earlier output no longer jumps back to the bottom.
Agents keep running after you log out or switch users: ForkMesh no longer shuts itself down when your desktop session's message bus restarts.
Right-click an agent folder in the desktop's Agents list to start or stop every agent in it at once.

An Import button above the Agents list brings in your Claude Code and Claude Desktop sessions, named as they are in Claude, with their whole conversation, and you can carry on any of them from ForkMesh.

sections.title: World
items: Stepping into a neighbouring World's hexagon is seamless: its hexagon is built ahead of time, people stay visible on both sides while you cross, and the World no longer blanks out or stalls after a while on slower devices.
Road edges now join continuously around the outer bike loop.
Riding the coaster in first person, your view now tilts, banks and turns upside down with your seat, and a look to the side stays put through the loops.
Walking out of an instance's World, such as OWASP BLT, onto the ForkMesh land next door now puts you in the ForkMesh World, with its people and town, without leaving the page or signing out.
Leaderboard Island's boards now stand on one ring, and each board refreshes only when you step onto the small glowing half-circle in front of it.

Move any World HUD button, such as Capture, Sound or an emote, between the top, left, right and bottom rails by dragging it or with the keyboard; it resizes to fit its new rail and the layout is remembered on this device.

sections.title: Settings
items: Closing the web status editor now returns keyboard focus to the control that opened it.

Settings > Data on the iPhone can save your home screen layout, news reader subscriptions and app settings to your ForkMesh account, encrypted, and shows everything ForkMesh keeps about you, your organizations and your repositories, with a full download and per-item delete.
A new Match the instance's theme option in Appearance makes the desktop and iPhone apps wear the colours your instance's admin picked.

sections.title: iPhone
items: With Status Page installed, tiny status dots now sit in the thin strip above the Dynamic Island, so you can see ForkMesh's health on every screen.
Link previews in shared rooms load only when you tap them, and private network addresses are never fetched.
On the iPhone Home screen, the number on each icon now sits beside the icon, so it no longer covers the name of the icon above it.
Merge all with AI on a repository's pull requests now reaches your desktop's copy instead of saying the desktop does not have that repository.
A walk now shows in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen as soon as you've been walking with ForkMesh open, and stays there when you lock the phone mid-walk.

The Agents list's Eagle view drops the agent circle on the left; each row's image tile now shows lines added and removed as a green and red border, the file count and a status dot in a small pill, and blinking dots for the agent's background tasks.

sections.title: Android
items: Notifications show no message text on the lock screen, and nearby #mesh alerts follow your notification content setting.
On Android, the first action on an agent's page is no longer cut off when the page has more actions than fit.

sections.title: Desktop
items: A phone pairing request now defaults to Deny, no longer jumps in front of your work, and expires after two minutes.
Drag the right edge of the expanded sidebar to make it wider or narrower; double-click it to reset.
An Actions run that stops because the computer is low on disk space now says to run Free disk space first, and its ping is filed as a disk problem.
A run waiting for your approval now says why it is held, such as a first-time contributor's pull request, instead of only saying the workflow has no changes.
Right-click the desktop's top bar to hide the Agents, Nodes or Actions grids, and right-click it again to bring them back.
Hovering a usage chart now shows the current account's usage bars with its account, terminal and reset-timer controls, the same ones the Usage page has.

The desktop debug bar shows log icons only for the log types you record, draws every chart at one small size with a live detail card when you hover it, and overlaps the status dots without captions, as on the phone.

On desktop, the prompt's chat preview now fills the top of the box with small avatars beside each line, its buttons float over the top-right corner with the resize grip at the right end, a third line is no longer cut off, and with #general or another chat room open the preview shows that room.

The prompt composer keeps its add button, files tasks from the model menu, and has a send to: button that posts the prompt to the chat channel you have open, such as #general; with the Chat page open, Enter sends there.
Pick a theme straight from the view menu at the top right, try the new Halloween theme, and drag the timers clock to the left, middle or right of the top bar.

sections.title: Server
items: Self-hosted instances show the platform changelog at /changelog, and their menus no longer show forkmesh.com's Company links.

sections.title: Server
items: Security reports sent to forkmesh.com/api/security/report, including from AI agents and scanners that read the code, now alert the maintainers at once and open a private fix task.

sections.title: Other improvements
items: forkmesh.com/features lists every feature again, with a count for each section and a mark on every feature that is a Market plugin.
In the dark theme, text on blue buttons is now easier to read, the repository filter shows a focus outline, and the phone menu button is easier to tap.

entries.title: Neighbours, stickers and runners
entries.pitch: Walk between ForkMesh Worlds, react to messages with stickers, and keep runners in hand from the desktop and the iPhone.

sections.title: Market
items: Feed is a Market package, with its own screens on iPhone and Android.
NEXUS and runners joined the Market.
The CRM moves a contact to Contacted every time you reach out to them.

sections.title: Calls
items: A missed-call line is posted when the caller hangs up before you answer.
Video calls you place to an iPhone now show the other person's camera and play their voice once they answer.
Call buttons fit small screens, and you can drag your own video to any corner of the call.

sections.title: Projects
items: An instance belongs to only one project.
Add your own instance from the Federated instances list.
An instance on a forkmesh.com address can reach its own domain, and an instance installed from a config file no longer removes itself when nobody signs in within five minutes.

sections.title: Chat
items: Stick stickers on messages.
Swipe left on a message for Message Info; your last sent message shows when it was delivered and read.
Each project keeps its own chat when you switch projects.
The iPhone no longer tells other devices the names of your private channels, so one project's channels stop turning up in another.
Chat on iPhone is snappier: closing Control Center no longer reconnects every conversation, and message lists, typing and the channel list redraw far less.

sections.title: Agents
items: Pause and resume runners from the new Runners pages on the desktop and the iPhone.
Your last prompt stays pinned above every agent transcript.
Scrolling back through a transcript no longer snaps to the bottom.
Review with AI uses the agent and model picked in the composer.

sections.title: World
items: Walk from your World onto a neighbouring instance's hexagon and see its scene, without reloading.
Visitors can walk into a neighbour's Office.
Walk into an instance's hexagon, such as OWASP BLT, and you stand in its real World: its members, repositories, buildings and bug terrarium, with ForkMesh's town next door.

sections.title: Settings
items: What's new in the app and forkmesh.com/changelog now show the same notes.
Instance and organization admins can add their own reactions under Settings, Reactions, GIFs & tips.

sections.title: iPhone
items: AUTO DJ plays a related song people liked on the next deck.

sections.title: Server
items: Issues and pull requests link up from Development and from "fixes #N" comments.
Mirrors fetch issue, pull request and discussion changes as soon as they are committed.
Delete branches one at a time or several at once.
Say thanks on any comment with the new gratitude reactions and Thank you sticker, reply with a GIF, or tip the author wallet to wallet with Solana Pay.
Issue search now looks through descriptions and comments, and the issue list stays quick with thousands of issues.
Pull requests whose code contains a byte-order mark or another invisible character are accepted and flagged instead of failing with a bad signature.
The code map no longer shows text files as binary at random.

sections.title: Other improvements
items: Hidden Unicode characters are stripped from every input on the web, desktop, phones and server.

entries.title: Face swap, a new Market and What's new
entries.pitch: Calls get face swap and background blur, the Market gets a fresh look, and the app tells you what changed.

sections.title: Market
items: The Market has a fresh look, with sorting, filters, usage numbers and one-tap install.
Packages you have installed now show as installed, every time.

sections.title: Calls
items: Face swap in video calls now covers your whole head, hair included, and follows your movements naturally.
Your voice changes to match the face you pick.
Blur your background during a call, or replace it with a picture of your own.

sections.title: Projects
items: A new project no longer shows repositories from app.forkmesh.com until you choose an instance for it.

sections.title: Settings
items: Your app version and build number now show at the bottom of the You menu. Tap it to see what is new.

entries.title: The Living Code City
entries.pitch: ForkMesh becomes a shared three-dimensional developer world backed by independently operated repository mirrors.

sections.title: Highlights
items: **Everyone enters the World.** Guests and members share the Town Square, see live avatar movement, and can use the embedded public World chat without leaving the scene.
**Resilient repository routes.** Public smart-HTTP traffic is proxied through healthy, signed mirrors with automatic failover and round-robin selection.
**SSH Git access.** Users can register an OpenSSH public key and clone or push through the permission-checked Git gateway; private keys remain on their own device.
**Non-custodial community rewards.** Contributors can fund the transparent public Solana pool directly from a self-custodial wallet. ForkMesh never stores contributor or node-operator private keys.
**Privacy-safe identity.** Clothing badges use optional approximate country, browser, and operating-system symbols without publishing raw IP addresses or precise location.
**Operational clarity.** World notifications, repository integrity proofs, security scan scope, and infrastructure metaphors link back to the technical state they represent.

entries.title: The Agent Mesh
entries.pitch: The release where ForkMesh starts to feel alive. Open an issue, hand it to an AI agent, and watch a real pull request show up — all without leaving the mesh.

sections.title: Highlights
items: **Built-in coding agents.** Assign any issue to Claude Code or Codex from the issue detail or quick-add box. The agent works on your connected fork and opens a pull request when it's done.
**A real terminal, in the app.** A native VT100 terminal renders every agent and workflow run with full color output and emoji.
**Legacy issue bounties.** This release originally added a custodial issue-bounty flow. That flow has since been retired: please do not send funds to historical bounty addresses.
**VS Code Marketplace plugin.** Optionally browse issues and kick off ForkMesh agents from your editor without installing the plugin in the base desktop app.
**Profile pages.** Click any node to see its full public profile — repos, identity, and version.
**Hardened by default.** Tighter signup and relay security, with auto-publish off until you say so.

entries.title: Autonomous Agents
entries.pitch: Collaboration stopped being a one-person job.

sections.title: Highlights
items: **Parallel agents, no queue.** Run multiple agents at once across your issues.
**Continue the conversation.** Pick a session back up where it left off, with auto-PR creation on quick tasks.
**Live activity indicators.** See which agents are working right now.
**Issues and PRs that talk to each other.** Merge a PR and its linked issue closes itself; sync straight to main with one checkbox.
**One-click delegation.** Send any issue to your agent of choice — pre-filled and ready to go.

entries.title: Identity & Rewards
entries.pitch: ForkMesh added optional community-funded incentives for healthy mirror operators.

sections.title: Highlights
items: **Guest-first access.** Visitors enter the world immediately; registered accounts use email, password, and email verification.

**Solana payouts and contributions.** Publish a self-custodial payout address or voluntarily fund the public mainnet-beta community pool with a direct transfer signed in your own wallet. ForkMesh never receives a community member’s wallet key.
**Rewards for mirroring.** Eligible, integrity-verified nodes may be selected for a community incentive; participation, payment, and financial returns are never guaranteed.
**Network presence, done right.** Mirror-sync notices moved into a proper network log, with live connection alerts.

entries.title: Collaborate Anywhere
entries.pitch: The web caught up to the desktop, and ForkMesh went mobile.

sections.title: Highlights
items: **Pull requests.** Signed patch submissions, browsable on the web and mergeable from the client.
**Actions.** Run shell-step workflows on push on your own desktop, with the latest live log one click away.
**Releases and tags.** See your tags, mark the current one, and cut new releases in seconds.
**Browse before you mirror.** Explore files, commits, and rich diffs (images side by side) — no clone required.
**ForkMesh on your phone.** Browse repositories, follow activity, chat, and submit signed collaboration updates. The mobile app is an access client; Git mirroring remains a desktop/headless-node job.
**Fork with intent.** Choose exactly where a fork lands in your working tree.

entries.title: Genesis
entries.pitch: The first commit. A bet that source code shouldn't be locked to a single forge.

sections.title: Highlights
items: **A distributed mirror network.** Local Git mirrors, signed identities, and a Cloudflare relay that coordinates without ever holding your objects.
**A public catalog.** Public repositories and clearly labeled external stubs, with actively mirrored repository bytes streamed over HTTPS from a selected healthy origin.
**Issues that grow with you.** Open/closed states, priorities, custom fields, a Kanban board, and milestones with progress bars.
**Commit history and diffs**, viewable right in the browser.

**Authenticated shared-key room chat.** Genesis shipped client-encrypted transport whose default passphrase the relay could derive. Current public channels intentionally retain that integration-compatible boundary; private channels and direct messages now add automatic device-recipient encryption beyond it. Persisted frames remain limited to 500 per room for 7 days.
**One-click hand-off to your AI tools**, baked in from day one.
